newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Mayor of Albanian town wants government to quit.
newsitem.headline: Mayor of Albanian town wants government to quit.

text.p: The mayor of the Albanian port of Vlore called on Friday for the government to quit over its failure to contain a month-long crisis over the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.

"They have done nothing to help the people. They must go," mayor Gezim Zile, a member of ruling right-wing Democrats, told Reuters. He was the first Democrat leader to suggest that the government should resign.
Demonstrators in Vlore, demanding the return of their lost savings, staged a 10th day of street demonstrations against Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi's government.

Three people were killed and 150 injured in clashes with riot police during anti-government protests in the town earlier this week. Destitute Albanians blame the government for allowing the dubious investment schemes to flourish.
In the town of Fieri, 40 km (25 miles) to the north, protesters marched through the centre, then skirmished with riot police on Friday.
They threw stones at the police who tried to push them back, but quickly broke through the cordon and marched noisily past the city hall, which was burned during a riot last month.
Later a small group of demonstrators set up roadblocks on the dilapidated road between Fier and Vlore, vowing to keep up their blockade until the Meksi government resigns.
"We want to separate from the rest of Albania, we do not recognise (President Sali) Berisha any more," one protester shouted at motorists trying to get through.

Four weeks of unrest have plunged the ruling Democrats into the deepest crisis of their five-year rule. Albania's south, once the more prosperous part of this impoverished Balkan state, has slowly slipped into a state of anarchy and chaos.
"I cannot sleep at night," said Zile. "This city is not safe any more. It is a very grave situation," he said.

Earlier this week a protester was shot dead in Vlore and two demonstrators died of heart attacks. On Monday, an angry crowd stoned a group of riot policemen, stripped them to their underwear and burned their gear.
The police quickly abandoned the town to criminals, thugs and smugglers. An off-duty policeman was killed on Wednesday, executed by two gunmen in what authorities said was a family feud.
The town narrowly avoided being put under emergency rule after local deputies appealed to parliament to think again.
"That would have been a disaster," said Zile. "If you send in the military this place will blow up."
In the chaos that has engulfed the region it has become impossible to tell which side starts the violence. Government critics say they are constantly harassed by secret police.
In Fier, several civilians who were spotted around the ruling Democrats' local headquarters were later seen among the riot policemen, having donned helmets and carrying shields.
In an attempt to contain the crisis the government seized $300 million in assets from two failed investment schemes and has promised partial refunds.
Privately, some officials doubt that cheated investors would see any of the money they have lost.
"There is no way anybody would get their money back. It's gone," one local official told Reuters, requesting anonymity. "But I cannot say that openly -- they will kill me."
